newsitem.title: USA: Southern to buy Consolidated Electric Asia stake.
newsitem.headline: Southern to buy Consolidated Electric Asia stake.

text.p: Southern Co said Wednesday its Southern Electric International subsidiary has agreed to purchase a majority interest in Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd in a $2.7 billion transaction.
Consolidated, one of the largest independent power producers in Asia, is now 60.4 percent owned by Hopewell Holdings Ltd.

"Under the agreement, CEPA (Consolidated Electric) shareholders will receive $2.1 billion from Southern and $600 million in dividends for 80 percent of the company. Hopewell will become the largest minority shareholder of CEPA," Southern's statement said.
Company officials were not immediately available to explain how this transaction would be carried out.
Southern did say the transaction is subject to approvals by the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong and CEPA shareholders.

"Combining the assets of Southern Electric International and CEPA will create one of the world's largest independent power producers, supplying electricity to the heart of Asia -- including three of the world's most populated countries -- as well as Europe, North America and South America," said Southern Chief Executive Officer A.W. Dahlberg.

Consolidated Electric Asia builds, owns and operates electric power generating plants in China and the Philippines with projects under development in Pakistan and Indonesia. It owns 3,995 megawatts of power generation with another 1,200 megawatts under construction and power purchase agreements covering an additional 2,640 megawatts.
The company was established in 1993 as a holding company for Hopewell's electric power projects.
Southern Electric owns 1,581 megawatts, with another 380 megawatts under construction. Southern Electric operates a total of 2,735 megawatts.
